clue.text: Young royal broke pincer taking fish

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

parts.note: ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A young prince has smashed some tongs while landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor or young prince is a petty royal personage, the usual sense of the diminutive word.

clue.text: Forward a bit of text

parts.note: 'a' as in 'fifty pence a kilo' means per, each

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to advance a short passage of writing, as in an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a mere article but stands for PER, as in prices quoted 'a kilo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of cheeky or presumptuous is a synonym of saucy, impudent behaviour.

clue.text: Fancy one cheeky gamine

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: cheeky suggests playful mischief, so the word gamine is mischievously rearranged

explanation.surface: A man taking a fancy to a certain impudent elfin girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to suppose or picture it in the mind, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cold grog redhead brewed for tourist spot

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: brewing mixes and stews ingredients, so the letters of grog redhead are churned up

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired drinker prepares a chilled rum drink to sell at a beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEDDAR GORGE is a limestone gorge in Somerset, England, a famous visitor attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset limestone ravine is one of England's best-known sightseeing destinations, so it is an example of a visitor attraction.

clue.text: Transfers allow artist to get established

parts.note: to let is to allow or permit
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock artist
something set is fixed or established

explanation.surface: Artists' transfers help a painter get started in business.
explanation.walkthrough: Letraset is a trademark for sheets of rub-down dry-transfer lettering, once used by graphic artists.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name was for sheets of rub-on lettering, so the product is a kind of decal or transfer.

clue.text: Not one against concept

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: Nobody opposes the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea or conception held in the mind is a synonym of concept.

clue.text: Little one almost gets a cake

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an infant or little one is a baby

explanation.surface: A toddler gets given a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A baba is a rum-soaked yeast cake, the rum baba.
explanation.definitionFit: The rum baba is a small sponge soaked in syrup, so it is an example of a sweet bake.

clue.text: A solid figure holding Italian flower

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape in geometry
IT is the usual abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: A statue clutching a bloom from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood and winter aconite are flowering plants, so the plant name is an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Oppositions against changing sheets

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of the word sheets are reordered

explanation.surface: Objections to swapping the bedlinen.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrasts or direct opposites in argument are contrary propositions, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Change relates to gallery dealing with property

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the word relates are reordered

parts.note: the word as printed; it carries one T more than the anagram can use
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A shift in how one connects with an art gallery when handling land.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed: RELATES has seven letters but only six (R, E, A, L, E, S) are wanted before TATE, so one T is surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings held as assets are property, which is what the American term denotes.

clue.text: Innkeeper's spirit's not good

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a ghost is a spirit; the 's here is 'is'

explanation.surface: The landlord's ghost is a malevolent one.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 's are 'is': the innkeeper is a ghost minus good.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who receives guests at an inn is the one entertaining them, a synonym.

clue.text: Trousseau's kept here behind artist?

parts.note: behind is a jocular word for the backside or bottom
a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A wedding outfit stored at the back of a painter's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun for one's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride-to-be traditionally stored linen and clothes for married life in the lowest drawer of a chest.

clue.text: Offer includes new contract for apprentice

indicators.note: includes means contains, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction

explanation.surface: A job offer that comes with fresh terms for a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: To indenture a trainee is to tie them by agreement to a master, the verb's old sense.

clue.text: He defends a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: A player protecting a match point.
explanation.definitionFit: One who argues in defence of a doctrine or cause is its advocate, the agent noun.

clue.text: Bolts shot catching bleary toper in trap

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so one group goes inside the other
shot here means ruined or worn out, so the letters of bolts are scrambled
a bleary drinker is befuddled, so the letters of the word toper are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fastening rods are fired at a sozzled drunk who is caught in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a heavy drinker. 'shot' and 'bleary' each signal a scramble, and 'catching' sets the jumbled drinker inside the jumbled fasteners, just before their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker or wire cage baited to catch crustaceans is a fishing device, an example of a snare.

clue.text: I provided weapons like Nelson

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to be armed is to have been given weapons

explanation.surface: A sailor boasting of having equipped the fleet with guns, in the style of the admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Lord Nelson lost his right arm at Santa Cruz de Tenerife in 1797.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's famous admiral had a single arm after his injury, so he is the example given.

clue.text: Goddess active at another time on the top of Etna

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active
then means at another time, not now

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A deity who was busy, once, on the summit of the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek patron of Athens, also spelt Athena, was a deity of wisdom.

clue.text: Puritanical American did what anyone with a cold might, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound of the phrase gives the answer

parts.words: did what anyone with a cold might
parts.note: someone with a cold clears the nostrils with a handkerchief, blowing it

explanation.surface: A prim American sniffled as a cold sufferer would.
explanation.definitionFit: A prudish, strait-laced person is called this in American slang, a fair noun synonym.

clue.text: Pig eats the whole tree

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
all means the whole

explanation.surface: A pig devours an entire tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow, especially a low shrubby kind, is the plant meant; the word is a name for it.

clue.text: Shelter attraction put up for group of islands

parts.note: lee is a sheltered place, out of the wind

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: a draw is an attraction that pulls a crowd

explanation.surface: A safe haven put forward for a cluster of isles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a Caribbean archipelago, so the name stands for that island chain.

clue.text: 6, for instance, contains meat for US party

indicators.note: contains means holds, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer at 6 across is a baba, an example of a cake
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A baba with meat in it is served at an American gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside picnic where seafood is cooked, typical of New England, is an American social gathering.

clue.text: Side by side with an animal crossing river

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece goes through the other

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: Walking alongside a creature fording a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things level with each other in a line are alongside, a synonym.

clue.text: Stick around inside like a dog

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes about the other

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
inside means in

explanation.surface: A command to stay indoors as a dog would.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things relating to dogs comes from the Latin canis, meaning hound.

clue.text: Always happy by middle of fen or marsh

parts.note: ever means always
glad means happy

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Always cheerful beside the heart of a fen or swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A low marshy grassland, like Florida's Everglades, is a kind of swamp or wetland.

clue.text: Extraordinary rule applied to small continental plot

parts.note: an are is a metric measure of land, 100 square metres, used on the Continent

explanation.surface: An unusual law governs a little European allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' signals the metric unit used in mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon or exceptional is extraordinary, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Dish served up for moderates?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a stew is a dish

explanation.surface: A meal dished out for diners who eat in moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics 'wets' were moderate Conservatives who opposed Thatcher's harder policies; the question mark flags the jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher dubbed her centrist Tory critics by this word, so it names that group of political moderates.

clue.text: Scheme to include lake in saltworks

indicators.note: to include means to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a salt pan, or pan, is where salt is produced by evaporation

explanation.surface: A proposal to take in a lake within an industrial salt site.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot or design for doing something is a scheme, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Conspiracy involving island with healthy cetacean

indicators.note: involving means enveloping, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A scheme on an island involving a fit sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large dolphin species, and dolphins and whales are all cetaceans.

clue.text: Flow's restricted, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word said aloud, sounding like another

parts.note: tied means restricted, as in tied down

explanation.surface: The stream is limited, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the definition is 'Flow' and 's links it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise and fall of the sea is a current, or flow, of water.

clue.text: Bar elects rogue and has a party

indicators.note: rogue means out of control, so the letters of bar elects are scrambled

parts.note: the words as printed; they lack one E that the anagram needs

explanation.surface: A pub chooses a scoundrel and throws a do.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is flawed: 'Bar elects' gives nine letters, one E short of the ten needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark an occasion with festivities is to have a party, an idiomatic phrase for the verb.
